metaTitle: Website Design for Structural & Civil Engineers | Hamid Ali Asad
metaDescription: WordPress websites for structural and civil engineering consultancies in Australia and the UK: project galleries, credentials and fee-proposal forms that bring in enquiries.
h1: Website design for structural and civil engineers
heroSub: A site that shows your projects and credentials clearly, ranks for “structural engineer” in the suburbs you serve, and turns visits into fee-proposal requests.
cardText: Project galleries, credentials and fee-proposal forms for structural and civil consultancies.
boxText: I build WordPress sites for structural and civil engineering firms: project galleries, service-area pages and enquiry forms that collect what you need to quote.

problems.title: Your best work is hidden
problems.text: Projects sit in a PDF capability statement or a slow gallery nobody opens on a phone. Builders and architects can't see quickly what you've done.

problems.title: Enquiries arrive with no detail
problems.text: A bare contact form means a round of back-and-forth before you can price anything. A good form asks for the address, project type and drawings up front.

problems.title: You don't show up locally
problems.text: People search “structural engineer” plus their suburb or town. Without service-area pages, those searches go to directories and bigger firms.

includes: Project portfolio you can filter by sector, with before/after photos and drawings
Service pages for inspections, design, certification and remedial work
Fee-proposal form that collects site address, project type and file uploads
Credentials, registrations and insurances shown where clients look for them
Service-area pages for the suburbs or towns you cover
Fast, mobile-first build so site managers can use it on site

faq.question: What should a structural engineer's website include?
faq.answer: Clear service pages, a project portfolio, your registrations and insurances, the areas you cover, and an enquiry form that asks for the site address, project type and any drawings. Those let a builder or homeowner decide quickly and give you enough to quote.

faq.question: Can you work with the photos and project list we already have?
faq.answer: Yes. I can organise existing photos, case notes and capability statements into a project portfolio, and tell you where a few extra photos or short descriptions would help.

faq.question: Will the site help us rank in our local area?
faq.answer: I set up the technical and on-page SEO, including service-area pages and your Google Business Profile details. Rankings also depend on competition and reviews, so I explain what to expect for your area rather than promise positions.

faq.question: How long does an engineering firm website take?
faq.answer: A typical 6 to 10 page site takes 2 to 4 weeks once content is ready. You get a fixed quote and a timeline in writing before work starts.

problems.title: Visitors don't know what you do
problems.text: “Fractional CFO” is still new to many owners. If your site doesn't explain what's included and when they'd need you, they leave.

problems.title: Trust is the whole sale
problems.text: Owners are handing you their numbers. Your background, qualifications and how you work need to be easy to find and easy to believe.

problems.title: Booking is awkward
problems.text: A contact form and a wait for a reply loses people. A calendar link or a short qualifying form gets the call booked.

includes: Service pages for fractional CFO, financial modelling, forecasting and valuations

faq.question: What should a fractional CFO website include?
faq.answer: A clear explanation of what a fractional CFO does, who it's for, how engagements work, your experience, and a simple way to book a call. Many firms also explain typical scope or price ranges so owners can tell quickly whether you fit.

faq.question: Should we show our prices?
faq.answer: You don't have to list exact fees, but explaining how you charge (monthly retainer, days per month, project fees) reduces calls from poor-fit leads. I can help you word it either way.

faq.question: Have you built websites for finance firms before?
faq.answer: Yes. My recent work includes the Longfield Financial Advisory site in the UK, including its Fractional CFO, Financial Modelling and Business Valuation pages, built from approved mockups in Elementor.

faq.question: Can you help with SEO for a finance firm?
faq.answer: Yes. I handle technical and on-page SEO and can set up location pages and an articles section. I'll explain which searches are realistic to target for your area.

problems.title: Marketplaces own your leads
problems.text: Listing sites bring buyers, but sellers who find you there may also find your competitors. Your own site is where seller leads stay yours.

problems.title: Owners want discretion
problems.text: A business owner thinking of selling won't fill in a long public form. Short, confidential enquiry forms and clear privacy wording matter.

problems.title: Listings are a chore to update

includes: “Sell my business” pages aimed at owners in your cities or regions

faq.question: How can a business broker get seller leads from their own website?
faq.answer: Owners search for things like “sell my business” plus their city, or how to value a business. Pages that answer those questions, a confidential enquiry form and a clear explanation of your process give them a reason to contact you directly.

faq.question: Can listings be confidential?
faq.answer: Yes. Listings can show a teaser (sector, region, revenue band) with full details released only after a buyer signs an NDA through the site.

faq.question: Have you worked with firms in this space?
faq.answer: Yes. I built the website for Longfield Business Group, a UK firm that acquires owner-managed service businesses, and its sister site Longfield Financial Advisory, which includes buying, selling and valuation pages.

faq.question: Can I add and remove listings myself?
faq.answer: Yes. I build listings as simple WordPress entries with fields for each detail, so you can add, update or mark them sold without touching code.

metaTitle: Website Design for Home Care Agencies (UK) | Hamid Ali Asad
metaDescription: Websites for UK home care and domiciliary care agencies: CQC rating displayed correctly, pages families trust, and carer recruitment pages that bring in applications.
h1: Website design for home care agencies
heroSub: A site that reassures families, displays your CQC rating the way the regulator requires, and helps you recruit carers, all easy for your office team to update.
cardText: CQC rating displayed correctly, pages families trust and carer recruitment that brings in applications.
boxText: I build websites for UK home care agencies: CQC rating displayed correctly, clear service pages for families and carer job pages.

problems.title: Your CQC rating must be shown
problems.text: Every CQC-rated provider has to display its rating clearly on its website under Regulation 20A. It needs to be the latest rating and easy to find.

problems.title: Families decide fast
problems.text: Relatives are often searching under pressure. They need to see quickly which areas you cover, what care you offer and how to speak to someone.

problems.title: Recruiting carers is constant
problems.text: Most agencies are always hiring. A jobs page that's hard to find or apply through costs you applicants every week.

includes: CQC rating widget placed clearly on the homepage and service pages
Service pages for personal care, companionship, live-in and respite care
Area pages for the towns and postcodes you cover
Carer recruitment pages with a short mobile application form
Clear phone and enquiry options for families on every page
An easy editor so your office team can update news and vacancies

faq.question: Do home care agencies have to show their CQC rating on their website?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Regulation 20A, CQC-rated providers in England must display their latest rating clearly and prominently on their website. CQC provides an official widget, and I add it so it updates automatically. Check CQC's current guidance for your service.

faq.question: What do families look for on a home care website?
faq.answer: The areas you cover, the types of care you provide, your CQC rating, how to contact you quickly, and a sense of who your carers are. Clear answers to those make a call much more likely.

faq.question: Can the website help us recruit carers?
faq.answer: Yes. A dedicated jobs section with a short application form that works well on phones, plus job details search engines can read, usually brings in more applicants than a generic contact form.

faq.question: Can our office staff update the site?
faq.answer: Yes. I build it in WordPress with simple editing for vacancies, news and team details, and show your team how to use it.

faq.question: Can WooCommerce handle quote requests as well as online orders?
faq.answer: Yes. Products can be set to buy online, request a quote, or both. Quote requests collect quantities and details and arrive with your team as an enquiry or a draft order.

faq.question: Can trade customers see their own prices?
faq.answer: Yes. Trade accounts can see customer-specific or tiered pricing once logged in, while the public sees list prices or a quote button.

faq.question: We have thousands of products in spreadsheets. Can you import them?
faq.answer: Yes. I import products in bulk from spreadsheets or supplier feeds, including attributes for filtering and attached documents such as spec sheets.

faq.question: Have you built sites for industrial companies before?
faq.answer: Yes. My portfolio includes sites for lifting, tooling and industrial supply companies in the UK and Australia. You can see them on this page and on my work page.
